line: Ten of Swords: Crowley's title, planetary attribution and place on the Tree, with his account of the card.

sections.title: What Crowley says the card is
sections.line: Title and ruler, as the chapter gives them (pdf 181, 222).

quotes.quote: The Ten of Swords is called Ruin.
The card is also ruled by the Sun in Gemini

sections.title: Its place on the Tree
sections.line: The Tens belong to Malkuth (pdf 181), which is in Assiah (pdf 181).

quotes.quote: These cards are attributed to Malkuth.
So far as the Sephira is concerned, it is right down in the world of Assiah.

sections.title: What the card figures
sections.line: His description of the card, not a divinatory reading.

quotes.quote: It shows reason run mad, ramshackle riot of soulless mechanism

sections.title: Conflicts and gaps
sections.line: The Tens group intro says there is now no planetary attribution to consider (pdf 181). The card's chapter names the Sun in Gemini, and the table agrees with the chapter. The record keeps the chapter's planet; the group intro is the conflict.

quotes.quote: There is now no planetary attribution to consider.
